title: Cauliflower, fresh, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Cauliflower is an edible vegetable from the Brassica oleracea var. botrytis family. When cooked with butter or margarine, it retains a tender texture and gains a subtle, buttery flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cauliflower is rich in vitamins C and K as well as folate.
There are several varieties: white, green (broccoflower) and purple.
Cooking with fat improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.
Ancient cultures used cauliflower as a remedy for colds.
It can serve as a low‑carb substitute for rice or potatoes.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Compounds such as glucoraphanin help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium contribute to normal blood pressure.

items.title: Cruciferous vegetable allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cauliflower.

items.title: High oxalate content
items.content: Large amounts can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Potential excess fat intake
items.content: Using too much butter or margarine can make the dish calorie‑dense.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cauliflower can be boiled, steamed, sautéed, or roasted with a modest amount of butter or margarine. It pairs well with garlic, lemon, Parmesan cheese, and herbs. Serve as a side dish or add to salads, soups, and grain‑free recipes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh cauliflower in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, loosely wrapped in a perforated bag. Cooked cauliflower should be stored in an airtight container for up to 3‑4 days.
